capture_engagement.description: Whether the engagement events (sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced) of the email are captured as analytics events of the recipient. Defaults to true. A project whose admin turned engagement capture off captures nothing, whatever the send says. A send by `template.id` takes it only in the beta for sending email from code.

distinct_id.description: Distinct ID of the recipient's person. The send and its engagement events are recorded against that person. Defaults to the recipient's email address.

from.description: Sender of the email, as `security@example.com` or `Example <security@example.com>`, on a verified domain of the project. Without it, a send with `template_key` goes out from the project's default sender, and a send by `template.key` from its template's sender. A send by `template.id` doesn't take it.

html.description: HTML body of the email your code rendered.

reply_to.description: Addresses replies to the email go to. A send by `template.id` doesn't take it.

subject.description: Subject of the email your code rendered.

template_key.description: Names an email whose content your code rendered, such as `order-shipped`, so its metrics, logs and status group under it. Letters, numbers, hyphens (-) and underscores (_) only. Send it with `subject` and `html` or `text`. PostHog sends the content as is and never stores it as a template. Once you upload a template under this key, these sends run through that template's workflow, so their metrics and logs group with the template from then on.

text.description: Plain text body of the email your code rendered. Without it, PostHog derives the text from `html`.
